text.p: Baxter International Inc president Harry Kraemer said Thursday the company is comfortable with the First Call consensus earnings estimates for 1997 of $2.36 per share and for 1998 of $2.70 per share.

"That's a very reasonable expectation," Kraemer said in an interview with Reuters after the company released higher second-quarter sales and earnings from continuing operations compared to year-ago results.
Shares in the Deerfield, Ill.-based medical products maker were trading up 1/2 at 58 on the New York Stock Exchange.
On Wall Street estimates that the company would generate sales in 1997 of about $6.5 billion, Kraemer said, "I think that's very reasonable."
Baxter will exceed its target of $300 million in cash flow this year, Kraemer said. "Being in the $400 million range I think is very reasonable," he said.
In the second quarter, Baxter's gross profit margin was 45.5 percent, up from 44.5 percent a year ago, and boosted by the recent acquisition of Immuno International AG.
"We will definitely exceed in each quarter 45 percent in terms of gross margin," Kraemer said.

The company's HemAssist blood substitute product is expected to receive European marketing approval soon. "We're right now expecting approval for that product in Europe in 1998 ... I'd say mid-year is reasonable," he said.

"Once we have approval in Europe, we would expect a 12- to 18-month period between that and approval in the United States. So ... we would expect approval in the United States (for HemAssist) by the end of 1999," he said.
Baxter is also progressing rapidly on its Nextran xenotransplantation project, which involves development of special animal organs for use as transplants in humans.

Conseco said agent recruitment is accelerating. "The number of career agents (at Conseco's Bankers Life and Casualty subsidiary) was 3,365 at June 30, 1997, up seven percent over the year-earlier level," Hilbert said.

"We expect the number of Conseco's career agents, independent agents and registered representatives to continue to increase, and that these trends, together with the introduction of Conseco brand advertising in November, will have a very positive impact on sales in the remainder of 1997 and beyond," he said.
Conseco will announce second quarter 1997 earnings on July 30, the company said.
For 1998, the First Call consensus estimate is $3.23 per share, a 22 percent increase over the 1997 consensus estimate, Conseco said.

"Over the near term ... Conseco's consistent profitability will continue to be driven primarily by the company's active and disciplined management of its diversified and predictable in-force businesses -- by its ability to earn its targeted investment spreads and to continuously improve its operating efficiency -- rather than by new sales," Hilbert said.
